paragraphs: I am Ben, and I like numbers and animals. This week I make a poster for my class. It has numbers for four animals. First, the rabbit. A rabbit has twenty-eight teeth. A rabbit can live for about ten years. Some rabbits sleep in a home under the grass. It likes to eat grass.

Then I write about two big animals from the sea. A shark is a fish, but a whale is not. A shark loses its teeth, and new teeth come. Some sharks have about three hundred teeth. The blue whale is the biggest animal in the world. It can be about thirty meters long. Is that long? Yes! It is longer than two big buses.

Last, the snail. Snails move very slowly. After the rain, Tom and I go to the forest. The snails are small, and some are brown. Tom and I count the snails on the grass and trees. We find forty-five snails on the grass. We find fifty-five snails on the trees. How many snails is that? It is one hundred! Tom writes the numbers in his book. Now my poster is good. I love animals, and I love numbers!
